findings.note: Second paragraph: 'The Alameda County code enforcement office inspects every hoarded house before a sale closes and blocks the closing until the house is cleared.' No ledger claim or source supports it. It is an invented local legal/procedural rule stated as a flat certainty (inspection of every house, closing blocked, cleanout required). It also contradicts the brief ('No local rules') and the statute-based framing that the authority decides case by case. High-risk unsupported claim.

Bullet 1 'Accumulated junk, debris or garbage that creates a fire hazard, as judged by the fire authority.' narrows clm:1 (fire, health, or safety hazards) to fire only and adds 'as judged by the fire authority', which is the clm:4 combustible-waste standard (fire chief or deputy), not clm:1. Restore 'fire, health, or safety hazards' and drop the fire-authority attribution from this bullet.

clm:4 is cited but its condition (combustible waste or vegetation that, in the opinion of the fire chief or deputy, could cause a fire or explosion or provide ready fuel to spread fire) is not stated; it is blurred into bullet 1. Add it as its own row in the ledger wording, or stop citing clm:4.

'Clutter by itself is not a code violation.' is a legal conclusion stated as certain with no supporting claim. The statute does not address clutter or hoarding. Reword to say only that the statute lists specific conditions and the local enforcement authority decides whether a home meets them.
